class.name: JarTerrainFeature
class.brief_description: Large, persistent objects (trees, rocks, structures) placed on the surface of a [JarVoxelVolume].
class.description: Features are placed on the volume's SDF surface, independent of the mesh resolution, so they are seen from afar and always stand in the same place. Around each viewer, space within the largest [member draw_distance] is divided into cells of [member JarVoxelVolume.population_feature_cell_size]; in every cell the surface passes through, each feature is placed as its own layer, in the order of [member JarVoxelVolume.population_terrain_features]: Poisson disc samples are tested against the mask and clusters, ray marched down to the surface, then tested against the ground rules. A feature keeps instances of the features after it out of its [member footprint], so list large things first (trees, then rocks, then bushes). Generation runs on worker threads and is deterministic per cell. Edits remove the features standing in the region they change, for good; [method JarVoxelVolume.remove_features] does the same for gameplay (chopping a tree), and [method JarVoxelVolume.get_features_near] lists them. The approach follows [url=https://jorisar.nl/blog/Population/]Population of a Large-Scale Terrain[/url].

members.member: If [code]true[/code], [member mesh] instances cast shadows. Scenes set this themselves.
With a batched [member scene]: distance in meters from a viewer within which the scene's collision shapes exist (one static body per cell, with the collision layer and mask of the scene's body).
Instances per square meter where the rules and mask allow them. Trees are typically around [code]0.001[/code] to [code]0.01[/code].
Distance in meters from the nearest viewer within which this feature is shown. The largest draw distance of all features also decides how far features are generated.

Radius in meters kept free around each instance: instances of this feature are at least this far apart, and features later in the list are not placed inside it. Cells are generated independently, so instances in neighbouring cells can occasionally come closer.
Mesh drawn for each instance, with one [MultiMesh] per cell: the cheapest way to show many features. Ignored when [member scene] is set.
Scene instantiated for each feature, positioned by its root [Node3D]. Use it for colliders, scripts or LOD setups; it costs nodes per feature, so keep [member draw_distance] moderate.
How [member scene] is used. See [enum SceneMode].

constants.constant: The scene is a template: each of its [MeshInstance3D]s is drawn for all features of a cell as one multimesh, between its own visibility range begin and end (levels of detail, impostors); its [CollisionShape3D]s become colliders within [member collision_distance]. Scripts and other nodes are ignored. Materials that include [code]res://addons/jar_voxel_terrain/shaders/jar_population.gdshaderinc[/code] switch levels per instance and can blend with the ground color.
The scene is instantiated for every feature (scripts, lights, anything else). Much more expensive.
